did_you_know.text: Did you know? When Mordecai heard about the decree of destruction, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the city, crying out loudly and bitterly. This is how Scripture describes his immediate response to the danger.
Did you know? Mordecai went as far as the king’s gate, but he did not enter, because no one was allowed to enter the king’s gate wearing sackcloth.
Did you know? Mordecai was not the only one mourning: in every province reached by the king’s decree, the Jews mourned deeply, fasting, weeping, and lamenting, and many wore sackcloth and ashes.
Did you know? When Esther heard that Mordecai was wearing sackcloth, she was greatly distressed and sent him clothes to replace what he was wearing, but Mordecai refused them.

Did you know? Esther did not settle for merely hearing about Mordecai’s condition. She sent Hathach to find out what had happened and why he was mourning, and Hathach went to him in the street in front of the king’s gate.
Did you know? Mordecai told Hathach the details of the decree, including the amount of money Haman had offered to weigh out into the royal treasury in exchange for the destruction of the Jews.
Did you know? Mordecai also gave Hathach a copy of the written decree issued in Susa, so he could show it to Esther, and he asked her to go to the king and plead for her people.

Did you know? Entering the king’s inner court without being summoned was punishable by death. The only exception was when the king extended the golden scepter; then the person who entered would live. Esther added that she had not been summoned to the king for thirty days.

Did you know? Mordecai warned Esther not to think that she could escape in the king’s palace while all the other Jews were in danger—in other words, that she could hide in the palace while her people faced destruction.

Did you know? Esther decided to act after a time of communal fasting: she asked the Jews of Susa to fast for three days, night and day, and she and her attendants would fast as well. Then she said, “I will go to the king... and if I must perish, I will perish.”
